extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and wire-service editors (readers of Associated Press dispatches)
extracted.subtask_description: A wire-service newspaper article reporting military, political and civilian developments during wartime; combines dateline/byline, attributed communiqués, battlefield details, and human-interest elements for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute claims and information to specific sources and outlets (e.g., 'Berlin broadcast quoted a Kharkov front war correspondent', 'the Russian noon communique, as recorded by the Soviet radio monitor here').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always identify where a claim came from (broadcast, communique, newspaper, correspondent, government office). Examples in text: 'command did not support Berlin propaganda broadcasts Friday...', 'the communique broadcast was delayed...recorded by the Soviet radio monitor here.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag unconfirmed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state when a reported claim lacks independent confirmation (e.g., 'There was no confirmation from any Russian source.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When enemy or third-party claims are quoted, note absence of independent verification. Example: 'German headquarters asserted that Nazi troops had occupied the main railway station in Kharkov... There was no confirmation from any Russian source.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Report counterclaims and propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Present opposing accounts and mark them as propaganda or contested when appropriate (e.g., noting Berlin broadcasts and Moscow denials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both the claim and the opposing response or lack thereof, and label obvious propaganda. Example: 'command did not support Berlin propaganda broadcasts Friday saying that Kharkov had been recaptured, it said Saturday that its offensive was spreading...' and references to 'Berlin broadcast' vs. Soviet communiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and byline presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear dateline and byline information (e.g., 'By the Associated Press. LONDON, March 14 (Sunday)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with source and location/date so readers know when/where the dispatch originated; several pieces show 'By The Associated Press' and city-plus-date headers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic orientation and distances
rubrics_metrics.description: Give precise geographic details and distances for places mentioned (e.g., 'Belgorod is the vital railway town ... forty miles northeast of Kharkov').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orient readers with town names, relative directions and mileage to major cities or fronts. Examples: distances among Kharkov, Belgorod, Graivoron, Kursk and Smolensk are provided repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify losses and materiel with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of casualties, tanks, planes, trucks, and other materiel, and attribute those figures to their source (e.g., 'About 400 enemy dead...','11 German tanks ... burned out ...' the Russians said).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting counts or estimates, attribute them (which side reported them) and, where appropriate, present as the reporter recorded it. Examples: 'the Russians said', 'the communique declared', 'destroying 15 German planes and damaging about 20'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct quotations from communiqués and speeches
rubrics_metrics.description: Include verbatim phrases or quoted passages from official communiqués, broadcasts, and speeches (e.g., quoted passages describing town destruction, or Ambassador Litvinoff's remarks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotes to show exactly what an official/public figure or communique said and to preserve tone and content. Examples: long quoted passages describing Vyazma's destruction and Litvinoff's statement on lend-lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note timing and delays of official broadcasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Record timing details about when communiqués or broadcasts were issued or delayed (e.g., 'The communique broadcast was delayed after its regular period.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out delays, irregular schedules, or changes in broadcast timing to help readers assess information currency and possible reasons for omissions or emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize military movements strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain strategic implications of movements or captures (e.g., 'loss by them of Smolensk would greatly disrupt their front and leave a large number of their southern positions open to a flanking attack').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond reporting positions, provide context about why a location or action matters strategically for the campaign or supply lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report civilian impact and cultural destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Document effects on civilians and cultural institutions with specifics (e.g., 'The German bandits ransacked and destroyed the local drama theater, the cinema, the museum... The German Fascist invaders also demolished the Vyazma Cathedral.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details on civilian casualties, rescues, forced relocations, and damage to cultural/historical sites to convey humanitarian and societal consequences. Example: '1,500 villagers rescued' and catalogue of destroyed institutions in Vyazma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human-interest anecdotes to illustrate broader themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use short anecdotes and scenes (civilian sheltering at a birthday party, guerrillas buying arms for food, chaplain awarded silver star) to humanize and illustrate larger wartime conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interleave human stories and vignettes with operational reporting to give readers relatable perspectives. Examples: birthday party sheltering, Yugo-Slav patriots buying arms in exchange for wine, chaplain's citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report operational and tactical specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe concrete operational details such as raids, air battles, numbers of aircraft destroyed or damaged, positions taken, and tactics (e.g., 'Red Army air force pounded the airdrome at Orel, destroying 15 German planes and damaging about 20').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the nuts-and-bolts of military actions (targets, weapons used, immediate outcomes) to allow readers to follow the tactical picture; attribute outcomes to sources where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite diplomatic, political and aid-related statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on diplomatic statements and political context, including material aid and official appreciation (e.g., Moscow papers giving prominence to Ambassador Litvinoff's remarks about lend-lease).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statements that touch on international relations, aid, morale, and politics to show broader implications beyond the battlefield. Examples: statements on lend-lease aid and its reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a variety of corroborating and regional sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw on multiple types of sources—radio monitors, foreign newspapers, government communiques, battlefield dispatches—and identify them (e.g., 'reported by the Soviet radio monitor', 'Bern dispatch', 'German language newspaper reported').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference and cite a mix of local, foreign, and official sources to build a fuller picture while making clear provenance and potential biases.
